title: Jak minął weekend?
focus: a simple story: perfective events in sequence, non-virile plurals, process vs. result

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Super! W sobotę pojechałam|pojechalam z siostrą|siostra do Zakopanego|zakopanego.
lines.en: Great! On Saturday my sister and I went to Zakopane.

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.en: I’m jealous! So what did you two do?

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Najpierw weszłyśmy|weszlysmy na Gubałówkę|gubalowke, potem zjadłyśmy|zjadlysmy oscypki|oscypki na Krupówkach|krupowkach.
lines.en: First we walked up Gubałówka, then we had oscypek on Krupówki.

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Wieczorem byłyśmy|bylysmy tak zmęczone|zmeczone, że zasnęłyśmy|zasnelysmy o dziewiątej|dziewiatej.
lines.en: In the evening we were so tired that we fell asleep at nine.

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.en: And you? What did you do?

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Nic ciekawego|ciekawego. Przez cały weekend malowałem|malowalem kuchnię|kuchnie i w końcu ją|ja pomalowałem|pomalowalem.
lines.en: Nothing interesting. I spent the whole weekend painting the kitchen, and I finally got it done.

minal.tags: verb · perfective · past · 3rd person singular · masculine
minal.why: Jak minął weekend?, literally “how did the weekend pass?”, is the standard Monday question. Masculine because weekend is a masculine noun. As in zasnąć, -nąć verbs keep ą only in the masculine singular: minęła, minęło.

pojechalam.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person singular · feminine
pojechalam.why: Perfective: a single trip, the first event of the story. Jechać, because they travelled by car or train.

siostra.why: Z + instrumental, “with.” Polish says “I went with my sister” where English prefers “my sister and I went.”

zakopanego.why: Zakopane is an adjective in form, so it declines like one: do Zakopanego. Its locative is the old form w Zakopanem. It’s the best-known town in the Tatra mountains.

robilyscie.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 2nd person plural · non-virile
robilyscie.why: Tomek is asking two women, Ania and her sister, so the non-virile plural. To men or a mixed group: robiliście. Imperfective, because he’s asking about activities, not results.

weszlysmy.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person plural · non-virile
weszlysmy.why: Wejść is w- + iść, and its past is just as irregular: wszedł, weszła, weszli, weszłyśmy. Wejść na + accusative is used for climbing a hill or mountain. Non-virile, because it’s two women.

you.f: Only women: weszłyśmy. With a man: weszliśmy.

gubalowke.why: Na + accusative for the destination: wejść na Gubałówkę. Gubałówka is the hill above Zakopane with the classic view of the Tatras.

zjadlysmy.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person plural · non-virile
parts: past stem of jeść (jad- before ł)
zjadlysmy.why: Perfective: they ate them all, the next event in the sequence. Before ł the stem is jad-; the virile form has jed-: zjedliśmy.

oscypki.why: Oscypek is a smoked sheep’s-milk cheese from the Tatra highlands, pressed into carved wooden moulds. The e of oscypek is fleeting.

krupowkach.why: Krupówki, Zakopane’s main street, is a plural-only name, so it takes the locative plural: na Krupówkach.

wieczorem.why: A bare instrumental used as a time word: wieczorem, “in the evening.”

zmeczone.why: Zmęczony is a passive participle used as an adjective. It agrees with the non-virile subject: byłyśmy zmęczone. Tak…, że… means “so… that…”.

zasnelysmy.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person plural · non-virile
parts: stem with -ną- (ę outside the masc. sg.)
zasnelysmy.why: The -ną- of zasnąć appears as -nę- everywhere except the masculine singular, zasnął. Perfective: the moment they fell asleep.

dziewiatej.why: O + the locative of a feminine ordinal: o dziewiątej, “at nine.”

robiles.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 2nd person singular · masculine
robiles.why: Masculine, to Tomek. Imperfective: Ania asks what he was doing, not what he finished.

ciekawego.why: Nic + adjective takes the genitive: nic ciekawego, “nothing interesting”; nic nowego, “nothing new.”

malowalem.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 1st person singular · masculine
malowalem.why: Imperfective: the activity that filled the weekend. Przez cały weekend goes naturally with the imperfective.

ja.why: Ją refers back to kuchnia, a feminine noun, so English needs “it.” Polish pronouns follow grammatical gender, not sex.

pomalowalem.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person singular · masculine
pomalowalem.why: Perfective: the job is done. Malowałem… i w końcu pomalowałem shows both aspects of one verb side by side: the process, then the result.

exercises.prompt: Two women: “We went into the shop” (wejść): ___ do sklepu.
exercises.explain: Wejść has the past stem wesz- (masculine wszedł): We + sz + ł + y + śmy.

exercises.prompt: Ask two men: “What did you do?” Co ___?
exercises.explain: Men take the virile ending -i, with ł written l: robi + l + i + ście.
exercises.hint: Robiłyście is for women. What changes for men?

exercises.prompt: Say about yourself: “I finally finished writing the report” (napisać): W końcu ___ raport.

explain.m: The result, so perfective: na + pisa + ł + e + m.
explain.f: The result, so perfective: na + pisa + ł + a + m.

exercises.hint: Compare malowałem… i w końcu pomalowałem, and check the learner setting.

exercises.explain: Nic + adjective takes the genitive: nic nowego.
Z + instrumental; masculine nouns take -em: z bratem.
